headline: The passport photo grew eyes
lede: Papers, Please-Min's procedural portrait stopped being decoration: the mini face on every passport is now compared against the face at the counter, and the booth says what disagrees — while a grey-haired photo stays legal, because time fades color and forgery changes features.

notes.text: PORTRAIT rides the rulebook from day 1: hair cut, face width, glasses and facial hair are compared; a forged photo flips exactly one and the deny names it ("PHOTO WEARS GLASSES, ENTRANT DOES NOT"). Day 7 now prints nine laws, and the wall still fits its own fit law.
New trap species: the aged photo. Same face, grey hair — convict it and you just failed the lesson that colors are never evidence.

Proof at two levels: paperscheck 8482/8482 with three new named mutants (rule deleted, trap de-aged, color convicts — all die); papersplay 25/25 in real Chrome, where honest papers paint byte-identical face-and-photo pixels and a forger lights its own feature band.
QA picked up BombDefuse's powered hum and a pause-crash fix on its own lane; the never-dry stage keep finding real gameplay at the bottom of the shelf.
